fit: methanolic Cucurbita pepo seed extract and measured stride length in a haloperidol rat model
assessment: Publisher Figure 4 shows longer stride at ascending extract levels than disease control. This applies to the extracted seed and animal model, with no toasted-oil or patient contrast.

fit: chemical measurements in culinary oil pressed from roasted pumpkin seeds
assessment: Some overlapping phenolic compounds were measurable in roasted oil. Quantities were small and variable and the study contains no gait data or extract-dose equivalence.

fit: isolated p-coumaric acid and measured stride length in a haloperidol mouse model
assessment: Two higher purified-compound groups showed longer stride versus disease control. Oil concentrations are much lower than the tested isolated doses, with no established transferable effect.

fit: Cucurbita maxima seed ethanol extract and differing rod-task results
assessment: Favorable rotarod retention contrasted with slower stationary-rod arrival for the highest dose on day 21. The study gives no stride length or oil comparison.

fit: soybean oil-containing pea protein and alginate gel beads designed for oral delivery
assessment: The authors report mechanical gel behavior and in vitro release. There is no patient swallowing comparison or known oil grade.

fit: soybean oil vitamin D gel and tested texture classification
assessment: Texture and consistency tests place a formulated soybean-oil carrier in IDDSI levels 4–5 according to the authors. No observed swallowing event or refined-oil contrast.

fit: cardamom named in an adverse-event table and case-specific symptoms
assessment: Cardamom is recorded with finger numbness. Multiple-herb dizziness and blood-pressure reports are different cases. No specific postural symptom is attributable to ground cardamom.
